title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: Count outcomes number doctor visits, published articles, insurance claims usually modeled first Poisson regression. Poisson model forces variance equal mean. Real counts often vary much (overdispersion), many data sets contain zeros Poisson distribution mean produce (excess zeros). ignore overdispersion, coefficient estimates stay consistent standard errors small. ignore excess zeros, model describes zeros poorly can mix two different processes: whether event happens , often happens (Cameron Trivedi 2013; Zeileis et al. 2008). Two standard extensions handle features. negative binomial (NB2) model adds dispersion parameter θ\theta, Var⁡(Y)=μ+μ2/θ\operatorname{Var}(Y) = \mu + \mu^2/\theta. zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model (Lambert 1992) combines point mass zero (“structural zeros”) NB count distribution. title: Negative binomial regression — nbreg
text: Starting values. \(\beta\) Poisson fit computed IRLS (working weights \(a_i\mu_i\)); \(\theta\) moment estimate \(\sum a_i\mu_i^2 / \sum a_i\{(y_i-\mu_i)^2-\mu_i\}\). IRLS \(\beta\) (\(\theta\) fixed): \(w_i = a_i\mu_i\theta/(\theta+\mu_i)\) \(z_i = (\eta_i - o_i) + (y_i-\mu_i)/\mu_i\), update \(\beta \leftarrow (X^\top W X)^{-1}X^\top W z\). Newton-Raphson \(\phi=\log\theta\) (\(\beta\) fixed): \(\phi \leftarrow \phi - U_\phi/H_\phi\) \(U_\phi = \theta U(\theta)\) \(H_\phi = \theta^2 H(\theta) + \theta U(\theta)\). Repeat 2-3 log-likelihood changes less control$tol, final IRLS pass final \(\theta\). Standard errors: \(\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\beta) = (X^\top\hat W X)^{-1}\) (treating \(\theta\) known) \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta) = \{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2}\).

title: Zero-inflated negative binomial regression — zinbreg
text: Starting values: \((\beta, \theta)\) NB fit (nbreg()); \(\gamma\) logistic regression \((y_i = 0)\) \(z_i\), fitted IRLS. repeat: E-step. Posterior probability structural zero, \(\tau_i = \pi_i / \{\pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta)\}\) \(y_i = 0\), \(\tau_i = 0\) \(y_i > 0\). M-step, zero part. Maximize \(\sum_i a_i\{\tau_i\log\pi_i + (1-\tau_i)\log(1-\pi_i)\}\): logistic regression fractional response \(\tau_i\), fitted IRLS \(w_i = a_i\pi_i(1-\pi_i)\) working response \(z_i^\top\gamma + (\tau_i-\pi_i)/\{\pi_i(1-\pi_i)\}\). M-step, count part. Maximize \(\sum_i a_i(1-\tau_i)\log f_{NB}(y_i;\mu_i,\theta)\): NB fit nbreg() prior weights \(a_i(1-\tau_i)\). observed-data log-likelihood changes less control$tol. EM never decreases log-likelihood; path stored loglik_path, warning given ever decreases. Standard errors come inverse observed information, \(-\partial^2\ell/\partial\psi\partial\psi^\top\), \(\psi = (\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\), computed analytic second derivatives observed-data log-likelihood MLE. \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta) = \hat\theta\,\mathrm{SE}(\log\hat\theta)\) (delta method).
